pr.title: Simplify the canonical clone method and the copy-like forms to copy
pr.author: dianqk

analysis.summary: GVN gains `simplify_aggregate_to_copy`, rewriting an aggregate construction whose fields are a one-to-one `Field(i)` projection chain of one common base place into a single `Rvalue::Use(Operand::Copy(base_place))`. The rewrite is guarded by same-nominal-type, field-order, enum-variant, and base-not-mutated conditions, and it must mark reused locals so their `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` are removed. The PR adds MIR-opt tests for each guard (different type, swapped fields, mutated base, enum same/different variant, storage-dead/index) plus end-to-end codegen/pre-codegen tests.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR GVN's `simplify_aggregate` only canonicalized individual field reads (e.g. `_2 = copy ((*_1).0: i32)`) and then kept the aggregate rvalue as field-by-field construction: `_0 = AllCopy { a: move _2, b: move _5, c: move _8 };`. It had no rule to recognize that all fields came one-to-one from the same base place and collapse the aggregate into a single copy. As the PR description states, an optimized clone ended up as `_0 = Foo { a: move _2, b: move _3, c: move _4 };` rather than `_0 = copy (*_1);`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically tempting/incorrect rewrite is to collapse any aggregate `Agg { a: base.0, b: base.1, c: base.2 }` into `copy base` merely because the fields look like projections of one base. That is invalid when (1) the aggregate's nominal type differs from the base place's type even if layouts match, (2) fields are used in a different index order, (3) the base place was written after the field reads but before the aggregate is built, (4) an enum aggregate constructs a different variant than the one read, or (5) the new copy would reference a local after its `StorageDead`. The correct implementation only rewrites after checking all of these conditions and records reused locals so their storage statements are removed.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR at/after GVN (including inlined clone bodies) where an aggregate rvalue (struct, tuple, or enum variant, `AggregateTy::Def`) has fields whose GVN values are `Value::Projection(base, ProjectionElem::Field(index, _))`, possibly nested through `Deref`, `Index`, `ConstantIndex`, `Subslice`, `Downcast`, `OpaqueCast`, or `Subtype`. Relevant variations: same/different nominal aggregate type, permuted field indices, mutable base place, enum aggregate with same vs different variant, and projection paths containing a local that is `StorageDead` before the aggregate assignment.
analysis.trigger: `simplify_aggregate` is processing a `Value::Aggregate`/`AggregateTy::Def` rvalue and every field value is a projection of one common base value, with `ProjectionElem::Field(index, _)` matching the field position one-to-one, and the reconstructed copy place has the same type as the rvalue. For enums, a `Downcast` on the source path must match the aggregate's `variant_index` (and is then stripped); a mismatched variant blocks the rewrite.
preconditions: All fields must correspond one-to-one and come from the same aggregate value: `Value::Projection(pointer, ProjectionElem::Field(from_index, _))` with `copy_from_value == pointer` and `from_index.index() == index`.
The copy source place must be reconstructible from a local via `try_as_local`, i.e. its assignment strictly dominates the current location.
The rvalue type must equal the reconstructed place type: `rvalue.ty(self.local_decls, tcx) == place.ty(self.local_decls, tcx).ty`.
For an enum, if the source path is a `Downcast(_, read_variant)`, either `variant_index == read_variant` (strip the downcast) or the rewrite is rejected.
Any local consumed by the new copy (including `Index` locals) must be inserted into `reused_locals` so its `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` are removed and no use-after-StorageDead is introduced.
pitfalls: Nominal type equality is required even when two structs have identical field types/layout; `all_copy_different_type` keeps `_0 = AllCopy2 { a: copy _2, b: copy _3, c: copy _4 };` instead of `copy (*_1)`.
Field order must match; `same_type_different_index` (a = v.b, b = v.a) keeps `_0 = SameType { a: copy _2, b: copy _3 };`.
If the base place is mutated after the field reads, copying it would read the new value; `all_copy_has_changed` keeps `_0 = AllCopy { a: copy _2, b: copy _3, c: copy _4 };` rather than `copy (*_1)`.
Enum variant must match; `enum_different_variant` (read A, build B) copies only the inner `AllCopy`, not the whole enum, while `enum_identical_variant` produces `_0 = copy (*_1);`.

Replacing an aggregate with a copy of a local that was `StorageDead` before the aggregate would be a use-after-dead. `remove_storage_dead` and `remove_storage_dead_from_index` assert `CHECK-NOT: StorageDead([[V1]])` before `_0 = copy [[V1]]`; `Index` projections also introduce a local that must be added to `reused_locals`.
The rebuilt place must use `tcx.mk_place_elems` with reversed projection elements collected while walking from the value back to its local.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt` tests with `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` and `// EMIT_MIR ...GVN.diff`, plus `CHECK-LABEL`/`CHECK-NOT`/`CHECK` assertions on the resulting assignment. Cover the positive case (`_0 = copy (*_1)`), a nested copy, a double-reference case (`all_copy_2`), and each negative guard: different nominal type, swapped field indices, mutated base, mutated-then-reloaded field (`all_copy_use_changed`/`_2`, marked FIXME), enum same vs different variant, and `StorageDead` removal. Use `#![feature(core_intrinsics, custom_mir)]` with `#[custom_mir(dialect = "analysis")]` to force an `Index` projection and a `StorageDead` before the aggregate. Add a `tests/codegen/clone_as_copy.rs` test (`-O -Cno-prepopulate-passes`, DEBUGINFO/NODEBUGINFO revisions) asserting `call void @llvm.memcpy` and no element stores, and a `tests/mir-opt/pre-codegen/clone_as_copy.rs` (`-Cdebuginfo=full`) test asserting the full pipeline folds nested clones to `_0 = copy (*_1)`. The `gvn_clone.rs` test additionally uses `-Zmir-enable-passes=+InstSimplify-before-inline` to establish the pipeline, but the transformation under test is GVN.
